entries.prompt: Render the same project mask with an INTERMEDIATE silhouette proportion, about halfway between reference1 and reference2. Reference1 is too narrow/tall, reference2 is too wide/squat. Do NOT simply repeat either extreme. Reference3 is the small original project design and the ultimate authority for the shape. The desired visible whole-mask bounding rectangle width/height is approximately 0.96. Keep the reference1 material finish, colors, camera, existing feature layout, wear and PHG game-prop shading. Only adjust the overall visible width relative to height to match the source's intermediate proportion. Keep all parts and features intact in their source positions; no additional horns, glyphs, grooves, new damage or anatomy. One full same mask centered on square native transparent PNG, clear generous margins, no halo or backdrop, no UI/text/floor shadow. Shape interpolation only; do not enlarge individual features or lengthen the nose plate.

Fine relief, grain and lighting are generated interpretations; no hidden geometry, UVs or rig fit is established.

attempts.prompt:
ROLE: Create one high-quality PHG-standardized biomask cutout from the FIRST reference, the exact existing project design A. FIRST reference is authoritative for this design, silhouette, proportions, camera, panel boundaries, palette, wear/damage and visible openings. Keep the same yaw, pitch, roll, perspective and only the surfaces actually visible in A. This is a rendering adaptation, not a new mask, canon certificate or new view.

ART DIRECTION: Cohesive Predator Hunting Grounds-like game-prop quality. Broad neutral key from upper/front image left, restrained opposite/front fill, soft controlled reflections and readable cavities. Physically plausible material separation, modest roughness hierarchy, restrained pits/hairline grain and clean antialiased contours. Keep steel, dark glossy parts, gold/bronze, lacquer, bone-like or wood-like appearances distinct where A actually establishes them. Do not convert the entire mask to generic chrome or cover it in heavy grunge. Preserve each established color region; if A is grayscale and no reliable same-mask color evidence is provided, remain grayscale. Environmental blue/red highlights from any style reference must not become permanent pigments. Quality comes from light/material/readability, never added identity details.

LOCKS: Preserve all existing major features, asymmetry, damage state, missing pieces, dark optical lenses, true empty holes, emitter side/count and relative placement where visible/resolved. Do not add horns, crowns, fangs, teeth, vents, screws, glyphs, runes, ornaments, new cracks, scratches that change the damage pattern, or a different nose/jaw/eye shape. Fine unresolved detail stays restrained. If a second image is provided only as a STYLE reference, borrow lighting/detail hierarchy only: do not borrow its shape, colors, horns, engravings, damaged eye or other identity features. Same-mask primary evidence, if supplied, is for visible confirmation; do not invent unseen rear/interior geometry.

OUTPUT: One detached empty mask only, with no wearer anatomy, iris, skin, dreadlocks, hair, neck, clothing, armor, weapon or background. Maintain A's documented partial scope: do not finish cropped/uncertain appendages or repair damage. Empty damaged openings remain transparent; a dark intact optical lens remains dark. Native high-resolution PNG with true transparent background via the tool. Ask for square canvas, entire object about 75–80 percent of the LONGEST AXIS, centered with generous clear native margins around every point and chin. No floor/cast ground shadow, labels, text, UI, frame, watermark, fake checkerboard, aura or duplicate mask. No CPU crop/resize/recolor/re-encoding.
